current.jp: 次の特急は何時ですか
current.kana: つぎのとっきゅうわなんじですか

structure_explanation.en: の links 次 to 特急, forming 次の特急 ("the next express"), which is the topic marked by は. 何時 (read なんじ, "what time"; read いつ it means "when") is the interrogative predicate with です. The particle か at the end turns the sentence into a question. The vocabulary focus is 特急.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: の liga 次 a 特急, formando 次の特急 ("o próximo expresso"), que é o tópico marcado por は. 何時 (lido なんじ, "que horas"; lido いつ significa "quando") é o predicado interrogativo com です. A partícula か no final transforma a frase em pergunta. O foco de vocabulário é 特急.

translation_literal.en: As for the next express (次の特急は), when/what time is it (何時)?
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao próximo expresso (次の特急は), é quando/que horas (何時)?

translation.en: What time is the next express?
translation.pt-BR: A que horas é o próximo expresso?

note.en: です links 何時 to the topic with a polite tone
note.pt-BR: です liga 何時 ao tópico com tom polido

objections.objection: The batch ruled that いつ / 'when' / 'quando' is the wrong reading and sense for 何時 here, and changed kana, romaji, both explanations and tokens[4].gloss accordingly (gloss went from "when / at what time" to "what time"). But both literal translations still offer the rejected alternative: lit_en "...when/what time is it (何時)?" and lit_pt "...e quando/que horas (何時)?". Two learner-facing fields still present the reading the fix declared wrong.
objections.auditor_hint: lit_en: "As for the next express (次の特急は), what time is it (何時)?" ; lit_pt: "Quanto ao próximo expresso (次の特急は), é que horas (何時)?"

current.jp: ネクタイを締めて出かける
current.kana: ねくたいをしめてでかける

structure_explanation.en: The sentence chains two actions with the te-form (締めて = te-form of 締める). This form links 'to tighten the tie' to 'to go out', indicating sequence: first tighten the tie, then go out. The target here is the verb 締める ('to put on/knot', of neckwear) applied to a tie, and を marks the tie as the direct object.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase encadeia duas ações com a forma て (締めて = forma て de 締める). Essa forma liga 'apertar a gravata' a 'sair', indicando sequência: primeiro aperta a gravata, depois sai. O alvo aqui é o verbo 締める ('colocar/dar o nó em') aplicado a uma gravata, e を marca a gravata como objeto direto.

translation.en: He puts on his tie and leaves the house.
translation.pt-BR: Ele coloca a gravata e sai de casa.

gloss.en: to put on, to knot (a tie)

note.en: て-form of 締める (linking to the next action)
note.pt-BR: forma て de 締める (ligando à próxima ação)

note.en: dictionary form of 出かける
note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 出かける

objections.objection: Only the parenthetical gloss of 締める was corrected; the ops explicitly said the earlier phrase was also affected. The same paragraph now reads "This form links 'to tighten the tie' to 'to go out', indicating sequence: first tighten the tie, then go out. The target here is the verb 締める ('to put on/knot', of neckwear)" - it teaches the rejected sense twice and then contradicts itself in the next clause. pt-BR has the identical problem ("liga 'apertar a gravata' a 'sair'... primeiro aperta a gravata, depois sai. O alvo aqui e o verbo 締める ('colocar/dar o no em')").
objections.auditor_hint: en: replace "to tighten the tie" with "to put on the tie" and "first tighten the tie, then go out" with "first put on the tie, then go out"; pt-BR: replace "apertar a gravata" with "colocar a gravata" and "primeiro aperta a gravata" with "primeiro coloca a gravata"

objections.objection: After the sense correction, the literal translations still carry the rejected sense: lit_en "Tightening (his) necktie, he leaves." and lit_pt "Gravata (objeto) apertando, sai." This contradicts the corrected tokens[4].gloss ("to put on, to knot (a tie)" / "colocar, dar o no (na gravata)") and the corrected translation ("He puts on his tie" / "Ele coloca a gravata"). This is a wrong lexical sense, not the acceptable literalness of the lit_* fields.
objections.auditor_hint: lit_en: "Necktie [obj] putting on, (he) goes out." ; lit_pt: "Gravata [obj] colocando, sai."

current.jp: 夕飯の後で食器を片付けた
current.kana: ゆうはんのあとでしょっきをかたづけた

structure_explanation.en: The time expression 〜の後で (after) marks when the action occurred: 夕飯の後で = after dinner, with で indicating the moment. Next comes the object 食器を (the dishes) and the verb 片付けた (tidied/washed), in the past. The order is time + object + verb, typical of Japanese.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A expressão temporal 〜の後で (depois de) marca quando a ação ocorreu: 夕飯の後で = depois do jantar, com で indicando o momento. Em seguida vem o objeto 食器を (a louça) e o verbo 片付けた (arrumei/lavei), no passado. A ordem é tempo + objeto + verbo, típica do japonês.

translation_literal.en: After dinner, the dishes [obj], (I) put away.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Depois do jantar, a louça, (eu a) arrumei.

translation.en: After dinner, I put away the dishes.
translation.pt-BR: Depois do jantar, guardei a louça.

gloss.en: to clear away, to put away (the dishes)

note.en: connective stem 片付け of 片付ける, before the past
note.pt-BR: radical conectivo 片付け de 片付ける, antes do passado

note.en: auxiliary た forming the past of 片付ける → 片付けた
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た formando o passado de 片付ける → 片付けた

objections.objection: The ops named the parenthetical glosses inside both explanations, but neither was touched. expl_en still says "the verb 片付けた (tidied/washed)" and expl_pt still says "o verbo 片付けた (arrumei/lavei)", so the explanations keep teaching the wrong action while the translations now correctly say 'put away' / 'guardei'. Explanation and translation of the same sentence disagree.
objections.auditor_hint: en: "片付けた (tidied/put away)"; pt-BR: "片付けた (arrumei/guardei)"

current.jp: このきかいのつかい方をしりたいです
current.kana: このきかいのつかいかたをしりたいです

structure_explanation.en: Once more the target pattern 〜方（かた）: つかう (to use) → つかい + 方 = つかい方 (way of using / how to use). この きかいの つかい方 = "the way of using of this machine", with この ("this") and の linking きかい to つかい方. を marks this way as the object, and しりたいです expresses desire: しる (to know) in the stem + たい (desiderative) + です, "I want to know".
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Outra vez o padrão-alvo 〜方（かた）: つかう (usar) → つかい + 方 = つかい方 (modo de usar / como usar). この きかいの つかい方 = "o modo de usar desta máquina", com この ("esta") e の ligando きかい a つかい方. を marca esse modo como objeto, e しりたいです expressa desejo: しる (saber) na raiz + たい (desiderativo) + です, "quero saber".

translation_literal.en: I want to know how to use this machine.
translation_literal.pt-BR: O modo de usar desta máquina [obj], (eu) quero saber.

translation.en: I want to know how to use this machine.
translation.pt-BR: Quero saber como usar esta máquina.

note.en: つかう in the ます-stem つかい, which joins 方
note.pt-BR: つかう na raiz-ます つかい, que se junta a 方

note.en: suffix 方 (かた) attached to the stem つかい → つかい方 "way of using / how to use"
note.pt-BR: 接尾辞 方（かた）anexado à raiz つかい → つかい方 "modo de usar / como usar"

note.en: しる in the ます-stem しり, before the desiderative たい
note.pt-BR: しる na raiz-ます しり, antes do desiderativo たい

note.en: たい, desiderative attached to the verb stem (しり + たい = "I want to know"); inflects like an i-adjective
note.pt-BR: たい, desiderativo anexado à raiz do verbo (しり + たい = "quero saber"); flexiona como adjetivo-い

note.en: です added to したい to make the tone more polite
note.pt-BR: です acrescentado a したい para tornar o tom mais polido

objections.objection: The whitespace fix removed the spaces from jp (now このきかいのつかい方をしりたいです), but both explanations still cite the sentence in its old spaced form: "この きかいの つかい方 = ...". The quoted string no longer matches the sentence the learner sees. This is the only record in the batch where the stale spaced citation survives.
objections.auditor_hint: replace "この きかいの つかい方" with "このきかいのつかい方" in both locales

current.jp: お母さんみたいな先生が好きだ
current.kana: おかあさんみたいなせんせいがすきだ

structure_explanation.en: The structure is [modified noun] が好きだ ('to like X'). The target みたいな appears in お母さんみたいな先生: お母さん (mother) + みたい + な modifies 先生 (teacher), forming 'a teacher who is like a mother.' This whole block is marked by が because with 好き (to like) the thing liked takes が. だ closes as the copula in the neutral register.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura é [substantivo modificado] が好きだ ('gostar de X'). O alvo みたいな aparece em お母さんみたいな先生: お母さん (mãe) + みたい + な modifica 先生 (professor), formando 'professor(a) que é como uma mãe'. Esse bloco inteiro é marcado por が porque com 好き (gostar) o objeto do gosto leva が. だ fecha como cópula no registro neutro.

translation_literal.en: As for a motherly teacher, I like one.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a professor tipo mãe (que parece mãe), (eu) gosto.

translation.en: I like teachers who are like a mother.
translation.pt-BR: Eu gosto de professores que são como uma mãe.

role.en: comparison noun (base of みたいな)
role.pt-BR: substantivo de comparação (base do みたいな)

note.en: stem of みたいだ, linked to な to modify a noun
note.pt-BR: radical de みたいだ, ligado a な para modificar substantivo

note.en: な form of だ, makes みたい modify 先生
note.pt-BR: forma な de だ, faz みたい modificar 先生

note.en: na-adjective 好き, predicative with だ
note.pt-BR: adjetivo な 好き, predicativo com だ

gloss.en: is (copula, here closing 好きだ 'to like')

note.en: neutral form of です/だ, closes 好きだ
note.pt-BR: forma neutra de です/だ, fecha 好きだ

objections.objection: Not covered by any op in this record, but it survives the patch and violates the same rule the batch is enforcing: 先生が好きだ has no は, yet lit_en says "As for a motherly teacher, I like one." and lit_pt says "Quanto a professor tipo mãe (que parece mãe), (eu) gosto." The が-marked stimulus of 好き is mirrored with the topic device, and the record's own expl states that with 好き the thing liked takes が. Shipping it alongside the が/を fixes in the same batch bakes in an inconsistency.
objections.auditor_hint: lit_en: "A teacher like a mother (が), (I) like."; lit_pt: "Professor(a) tipo mãe (が), (eu) gosto."
